title: RushHour: A Dynamically Reconfigurable Lattice-Surgery Architecture
authors: Nathaniel Tornow, Aleksandra Świerkowska, Peter Wegmann, Pramod Bhatotia
abstract: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires efficient lattice surgery (LS), so that large algorithms fit on resource-constrained quantum chips. Existing approaches, however, are rigid: qubits, routing space, and resource states are allocated ahead of execution, which prevents running on small chips, leaves statically scheduled executions with large time overheads, and fixes each design at a single area of the space-time trade-off.   We present dynamic LS, which enables efficient reconfiguration of the ancilla space, just-in-time allocation of resource states, and dynamic rotations of logical qubits, thereby spanning the entire space-time trade-off with a single, unified approach. We realize dynamic LS with RushHour through a hardware-compiler co-design: the RushHour ISA formalizes and programs our dynamic lattice model, the Lattice Management Unit abstracts dynamic lattice management and performs efficient lattice reconfiguration, and the RushHour Compiler compiles logical circuits for physical chips into optimized ISA programs while pipelining instructions.   We evaluate RushHour against six state-of-the-art compilers and two resource models. On the smallest chips, 86% of benchmarks run only with RushHour, while existing approaches require 1.2-3.5$\times$ larger chips. On space-constrained early-FTQC chips, RushHour runs a median 2.0-7.2$\times$ faster than the best feasible alternative, while achieving results comparable to the state of the art on very large chips. RushHour's constructive results run 4.8$\times$ from an idealized-machine resource limit.
summary: This paper introduces RushHour, a novel hardware-compiler co-design for performing lattice surgery in fault-tolerant quantum computing. It overcomes the rigidity of existing methods by enabling dynamic reconfiguration of the quantum lattice in real-time. This results in significantly improved resource efficiency, allowing complex quantum algorithms to run on much smaller and faster physical quantum chips.
main_problem: Achieving practical fault-tolerant quantum computing requires efficient lattice surgery (LS) to fit large algorithms onto resource-constrained quantum chips.
main_result: The proposed RushHour architecture significantly improves resource utilization, enabling benchmarks to run on much smaller chips and achieving median speedups of 2.0-7.2$	imes$ on space-constrained hardware.
method: The authors propose a hardware-compiler co-design called RushHour, which formalizes dynamic lattice management via a new ISA and a Lattice Management Unit (LMU).
model_or_system: The system models fault-tolerant quantum computation using the surface code, where logical operations are performed via dynamic lattice surgery (LS) on patches of physical qubits.
key_observables: Space-time trade-off, benchmark success rate on small chips, execution time (speedup factor), and resource footprint.
important_parameters: Chip size constraints, logical error exposure, and the efficiency of dynamic reconfiguration (achieved in a single round).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that dynamic lattice management can be abstracted and scheduled efficiently by the compiler, allowing for non-blocking reconfigurations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between static vs. dynamic LS, the performance advantage of RushHour across different chip sizes, and the detailed structure of the dynamic lattice configuration ($\Sigma$).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of static LS, proposes the dynamic LS model, details the RushHour ISA and LMU components, and concludes with extensive benchmarking comparing RushHour against multiple state-of-the-art compilers.
why_interesting: While focused on superconducting/trapped-ion architectures, the core concepts of dynamic resource management, scheduling, and hardware-software co-design are highly relevant to optimizing complex quantum control protocols.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
